idea-plugin.name: DTT - Memory Safety Analyzer
idea-plugin.description:
Real-time Memory Safety Analysis for C++

DTT (Dependent Type Tracking) catches memory safety bugs as you type — before they become runtime crashes.

What DTT Detects

  • Null pointer dereferences — int* p = nullptr; *p = 1;
  • Use-after-move — auto v2 = std::move(v1); v1.push_back(1);
  • Dangling pointers — int* p = &vec[0]; vec.push_back(1); *p;
  • Buffer overflows — int arr[10]; arr[10] = 1;
  • Iterator invalidation — using iterators after container modification

Features

  • Inline error highlighting with red/yellow underlines
  • Gutter icons for at-a-glance issue visibility
  • Integration with Problems tool window
  • Configurable analysis strictness
  • Cross-platform: Linux, macOS, Windows

How It Works

DTT is a Clang compiler plugin that performs deep static analysis. Unlike pattern-matching linters, DTT understands C++ semantics — it tracks pointer states through control flow and knows which operations invalidate iterators.

Requirements

  • Clang 18+ (with plugin support)
  • DTT plugin library (auto-detected or manually configured)

Getting Started

  1. Install the plugin
  2. Configure clang path in Settings → Tools → DTT
  3. Open a C++ file — analysis runs automatically!
